examples.problem:
Let $V=\mathcal{C}\left[0,1\right]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $\left[0,1\right],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
\langle x(t),y(t) \rangle = \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} x(t) y(t) \, \textrm{d}t.
$$

Given that $x(t) = kt^2+3t$ and $y(t) = t$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ in $V,$ find the value of $k.$
examples.worked_solution:
Since $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(k{t}^{2}+3t)(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(k{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\frac{k{t}^{4}}{4}+{t}^{3}){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{4}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $\langle x(t), y(t) \rangle = 0$ and solve for $k\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & =0 \\ \frac{k}{4}+1 & =0 \\ \frac{k}{4} & =-1 \\ k & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(-1)y(-1)+x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2).
$$

If $p(t)=2+kt$ and $q(t)=t-{t}^{2}$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $p(t)$ and $q(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(-1)q(-1)+p(1)q(1)+p(2)q(2) \\  & =(2-k)(-1-1)+(2+k)(1-1)+(2+2k)(2-4) \\  & =(-4+2k)+0+(-4-4k) \\  & =-8-2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =0 \\ -8-2k & =0 \\ 2k & =-8 \\ k & =-4\end{aligned}
$$
